payload.summary: The archived candidate refactored the inline module-level binding scan in lookup_python_module_declaration into a call to a helper _scan_module_level_bindings(node, declared_name, candidates, uncertain) but never defined that function anywhere in the file. Consequently the final candidate raises NameError at declarations.py:144 whenever a module-body node is neither a ClassDef/FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef nor an Import/ImportFrom. The second public-check run (exit 1) confirms this directly: collection succeeds, 19 passed / 2 failed, both failures being 'NameError: name _scan_module_level_bindings is not defined' in the wrapped-locals and conservative matrix groups. The first public-check run (exit 2) showed a SyntaxError at a 'lambda: nonlocal_marker := None' line that appears in neither the archived candidate nor the baseline; the edit history (two edit-intent/edit-completed pairs with distinct intermediate hashes) indicates that syntax error came from a superseded intermediate edit state, not the final archived candidate. The observed defects are fully explained by the visible candidate source and public-check outputs; no withheld private defect is inferred. I did not acquire the current text of imports/members.py or tests/context/python/modules/test_selection.py, so consumer-side behavior is unverified.

findings.message: The candidate invokes _scan_module_level_bindings(node, declared_name, candidates, uncertain) in the non-class/function/non-import branch of the module-body loop, but no definition of _scan_module_level_bindings exists in the candidate file (or in the current bindings.py it depends on). This is a guaranteed NameError at runtime for any module whose body contains such a node.

The second public-check run (exit_code 1) matches the final candidate exactly: module collection succeeds and '2 failed, 19 passed', with both failures being 'NameError: name _scan_module_level_bindings is not defined' at declarations.py:144, occurring in the wrapped-locals and conservative groups of test_declared_namespace_matrix.

The local-scopes and targets groups passed only because their top-level body nodes are ClassDef/FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef or Import/ImportFrom, which hit 'continue' and never reach the undefined _scan_module_level_bindings call. Passing public checks therefore do not exercise or prove the refactored non-name-binding scan; the 2 failing groups are the ones whose module-level compound statements (e.g. conditional/loop bodies, handler guards) require that scan. This is consistent with the task's concern that canonical lookup must correctly handle module control flow with unrelated local namespaces.

The first public-check run (exit_code 2) reported a SyntaxError at 'lambda: nonlocal_marker := None,' (line 148), a line present in neither the archived candidate text nor the baseline. Given the edit history shows two separate edit-intent/edit-completed pairs with distinct intermediate content hashes (d3e0a9... -> 333a72...), this syntax error most plausibly arose from a superseded intermediate edit state rather than the final archived candidate. I cannot fully rule out an alternate explanation without the exact per-run file hash mapping, which is not provided.

The current modules/bindings.py contract (non_name_binding / iter_non_name_bindings) is unchanged by the candidate (identity 112152... matches the supplied baseline) and does not define or export _scan_module_level_bindings, confirming the helper is genuinely absent rather than supplied by the dependency. The inline baseline behavior that the candidate removed (ast.walk over non-declaration module-level nodes) is what the missing helper was meant to encapsulate.
